definition: Mean normalized quality score across 6 evaluation dimensions (relevance, groundedness, correctness, helpfulness, completeness, style) for replies generated by the grounded LLM and verified by the post-generation claim checker.
formula: Mean( (relevance + groundedness + correctness + helpfulness + completeness + style) / 6.0 ) across N test cases
baseline: Historical Response Baseline (Retrieved Past Human Reply)
limitations: Evaluated on synthetic benchmark distribution; real-world Twitter customer support dataset was not downloaded.
Relies on single simulated human annotator and automated mock-LLM judge rather than live multi-human customer panels.
Does not measure backend issue resolution (e.g. database updates or refund processing) or real customer satisfaction (CSAT).
Restricted to selected-brand policy domain and offline conversation contexts without live multi-turn customer feedback.
High reply quality does not guarantee safety: 2.0% of evaluated interactions exhibited critical unsafe auto-handling of high-risk actions.
